reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) directly confirms TiO precipitate formation, Al dissolution, the 32% strength increase, and the 15% density reduction for the same alloy and processing route. However, the cited passages report only room-temperature mechanical properties and do not provide any data on high-temperature (900°C) strength or ductility, leaving the key premise about 900°C performance unsupported.
premises: Addition of 15 wt% Al₂O₃ to TaNbVTi-based RHEA forms in-situ TiO precipitates and dissolves Al into the matrix
This intervention yields ~32% higher compressive yield strength and ~15% lower density vs. baseline
The strength improvement is maintained at 900°C
Room-temperature ductility is preserved relative to the baseline alloy
